stories.headline: Anthropic Cuts Off Claude Subscriptions for Third-Party Tools Like OpenClaw Starting April 4

key_facts.fact: Starting April 4 at 12pm PT, Claude subscriptions will no longer cover usage on third-party agent tools like OpenClaw
Boris Cherny, head of Claude Code at Anthropic, said subscriptions were not built for the usage patterns of third-party tools and cited capacity strain
A single OpenClaw agent running for one day can burn $1,000 to $5,000 in API-equivalent costs on a $200 Max subscription
Affected subscribers will receive a one-time credit equal to their monthly subscription price; discounted usage packages and API keys remain available

OpenClaw creator Peter Steinberger accused Anthropic of absorbing features into its closed system before blocking alternatives, but released cache efficiency improvements to help users minimize API costs
OpenAI continues supporting OpenClaw, positioning itself as an alternative provider for agent-driven workflows

stories.headline: OpenAI Reshuffles Leadership: COO Lightcap Shifts to Special Projects, Simo and Rouch on Leave

key_facts.fact: COO Brad Lightcap transitions to a new 'special projects' role overseeing complex deals and investments, reporting directly to Sam Altman
Fidji Simo, OpenAI's CEO of Applications, takes medical leave for a neuroimmune condition called POTS; Greg Brockman will oversee product in her absence
CMO Kate Rouch steps down to focus on cancer recovery after being diagnosed with late-stage breast cancer roughly 1.5 years ago; former Meta CMO Gary Briggs steps in as interim
Chief Revenue Officer Denise Dresser takes over most of Lightcap's responsibilities and reports directly to Simo
The reshuffle comes as OpenAI prepares for an IPO and has recently closed a record $122B funding round at an $853B valuation

stories.headline: Meta Pauses Work With AI Data Vendor Mercor After Major Supply-Chain Breach; OpenAI Investigating

key_facts.fact: Meta has paused all work with Mercor, a leading AI training data vendor valued at $10B, while investigating a security breach linked to the LiteLLM open-source library
The breach was linked to hacking group ShinyHunters/TeamPCP who offered to sell 200+ GB of database data, nearly 1 TB of source code, and 3 TB of video from Mercor
Mercor reportedly paid a ransom to ShinyHunters to purchase the stolen data; the listing was removed from the breach site
OpenAI is investigating the security incident to assess how its proprietary training data may have been exposed; other AI labs are also reevaluating relationships with Mercor
Mercor confirmed the attack internally on March 31; the breach potentially exposed how major AI companies actually train their models

stories.headline: Anthropic Files to Create AnthroPAC, Employee-Funded Political Action Committee

key_facts.fact: Anthropic filed a statement of organization with the FEC on April 3 to create AnthroPAC, a traditional corporate PAC (not a super PAC)
AnthroPAC is funded exclusively by voluntary employee contributions capped at $5,000; it will be overseen by a bipartisan board of directors
The PAC plans to donate to candidates from both parties in the midterms who align with Anthropic's interests in shaping federal AI policy
AI companies have poured more than $300 million into 2026 midterm races; Anthropic-backed Public First has already spent $2.26M in Democratic and $964K in Republican primaries
Aggregated Anthropic employee donation data shows 99.8% going to Democrats and 0.16% to Republicans, raising skepticism about the bipartisan claim

stories.headline: OpenAI Reveals Superapp Strategy: Merging ChatGPT, Codex, and Atlas Browser Into One Agent Platform

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is consolidating ChatGPT, its Codex coding platform, and its Atlas AI-powered web browser into a single desktop superapp focused on agentic AI
Codex product lead Alexander Embiricos said the goal is to bring Codex to ChatGPT's 900 million users without forcing people to learn anything new: 'No modes for us. That is the goal'

Codex head Thibault Sottiaux says the AI transformation of engineering will extend to all knowledge work within six months: 'I get more coding done than ever before, yet I don't actually write a single line of code anymore'
Codex now serves over 2 million weekly users, up 5x in three months, with usage growing more than 70% month over month
OpenAI is shutting down 'side bets' like Sora to redirect resources toward the superapp and agentic capabilities

stories.headline: Generalist Releases GEN-1 Embodied AI Model With 99% Task Success Rate, 3x Faster Than SOTA

key_facts.fact: GEN-1 achieves 99% success rate on multiple high-dexterity tasks (phone packing, box folding, vacuum servicing) where previous GEN-0 model reached only 64%
GEN-1 completes tasks approximately 3x faster than prior state of the art — folds boxes in 12.1 seconds vs ~34 seconds for GEN-0, packs phones in 15.5 seconds (2.8x faster)
The model requires only approximately 1 hour of robot-specific data to adapt to a new task and embodiment, achieving comparable performance to GEN-0 with 10x less task-specific data
Generalist's proprietary training dataset has grown to over 500,000 hours of high-fidelity physical interaction data, up from 270,000 hours in November
Generalist raised $140M at a $440M valuation in 2025 and uses low-cost wearable 'data hands' pincer devices worn by humans to capture training data far more efficiently than traditional teleoperation

stories.headline: OpenAI Fully Retires GPT-4o From All ChatGPT Plans as Usage Drops to 0.1%

key_facts.fact: GPT-4o was fully retired from all ChatGPT plans on April 3, 2026, including Business, Enterprise, and Edu customers who had retained access in Custom GPTs
Only 0.1% of users were still choosing GPT-4o each day before retirement, with the vast majority having shifted to GPT-5.2
GPT-4o remains available through the API; the retirement only affects ChatGPT product access
User feedback from those who preferred GPT-4o's conversational warmth directly shaped improvements to personality and creative ideation in GPT-5.1 and GPT-5.2

stories.headline: Microsoft Says Copilot Hit 'Pretty Big Audacious' Sales Goals in Q3 After Strategy Pivot

key_facts.fact: Microsoft commercial CEO Judson Althoff told staff that Copilot sales hit 'some pretty big audacious goals' in the quarter ending March 2026
Microsoft pivoted its strategy from bundling Copilot for free to actively selling paid subscriptions after disclosing in January that only 3% of customers were paying
The strategy shift came in response to Wall Street analyst pressure over Copilot monetization and AI return on investment concerns
Althoff said he feels 'very confident' in fresh ambitious targets set for the June quarter

stories.headline: Musk Requires Banks Seeking SpaceX IPO Roles to Subscribe to Grok and Advertise on X

key_facts.fact: Elon Musk is requiring banks and law firms involved in SpaceX's IPO to purchase subscriptions to Grok, his AI chatbot, as a condition for advisory roles
Some banks have agreed to spend tens of millions annually integrating Grok into their IT systems; Musk also requested banks advertise on X but was more flexible on that demand
Lead banks include Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Citigroup, Royal Bank of Canada, Mizuho, and Macquarie Group
SpaceX acquired xAI (Grok's parent) in February for $250B, consolidating the companies; the IPO targets a valuation above $2 trillion with a potential $75B raise

stories.headline: Utah Launches First US Pilot Allowing AI Chatbot to Renew Psychiatric Prescriptions Without a Doctor

key_facts.fact: Utah's Commerce Department approved a 12-month pilot allowing Legion Health's AI chatbot to autonomously renew prescriptions for 15 low-risk psychiatric medications including Prozac, Zoloft, Wellbutrin, and Lexapro at $19/month
The first 250 prescriptions will be monitored by a licensed physician, and the system must achieve a 98% approval rate before operating without immediate oversight
Controlled substances like Adderall are excluded; patients must be 'stable' with no recent medication changes or psychiatric hospitalization within one year
Legion Health is a Y Combinator-backed startup; Utah is the first US state to allow an AI chatbot to independently renew drug prescriptions
Security researchers have already exposed vulnerabilities in a similar Utah AI prescription pilot (Doctronic), including generating vaccine conspiracy content and tripling opioid dosages

stories.headline: UBTech Offers Up to $18M to Recruit Chief Scientist for Humanoid Robot AI Roadmap

key_facts.fact: UBTech is offering annual pay of up to 124 million yuan (~$18M), with a floor of 15 million yuan (~$2.18M), structured as a mix of cash, benefits, and equity.
The chief scientist will architect UBTech's embodied intelligence roadmap, focusing on vision-language-action models, manipulation learning, and transitioning lab research to real-world applications.
UBTech's 2025 revenue reached 2.01 billion RMB, a 53.3% year-over-year increase, with humanoid products and services now comprising 41% of total revenue—a twentyfold increase.
Airbus purchased UBTech's Walker S2 humanoids for aircraft manufacturing in January 2026, validating real-world industrial deployment.

The salary is unprecedented in China's AI industry, which has historically eschewed the mega pay packages offered by firms like Meta. Competitors like Geekplus-W hired Tsinghua's Dr. Zhao Hao as chief scientist in February.

stories.headline: Meta's Ohio Data Center Seeks $3B in First-of-Its-Kind Loan Bundling Building and Power Assets

key_facts.fact: Meta's 'Project Walleye' Ohio data center is seeking $3 billion in loans in a first-of-its-kind financing structure where lenders fund both the building and the power assets in a single deal.
The deal is innovative because data center financing traditionally separates building costs and energy/power system costs into separate lending arrangements.
Meta has separately tapped Pimco and Blue Owl for $29 billion in broader data center financing, and recently revised its El Paso data center investment to $10 billion for 1 GW capacity.

stories.headline: Iranian Strikes Render Two AWS Zones 'Hard Down' in Bahrain and Dubai; Amazon Tells Staff to Deprioritize

key_facts.fact: An internal Amazon memo states that one availability zone each in Dubai and Bahrain is 'hard down' while another in each location is 'impaired but functioning.'
The memo directed that 'services should not expect to be operating with normal levels of redundancy' and should be 'scaled to the minimal footprint required to support customer migration.'
Amazon said it has no timeline for when the Dubai and Bahrain regions will return to normal operations, and is actively helping customers migrate workloads to alternate AWS regions.
A Wednesday strike caused a fire at Amazon's Bahrain facilities, with multiple hits sustained in the UAE, as the conflict nears its sixth week.
The IRGC has threatened Microsoft, Google, and Apple infrastructure as economic targets in the Gulf region, naming 18 US tech companies as 'legitimate targets.'

stories.headline: Global Semiconductor Sales Hit $88.8B in February, Up 61.8% YoY, on Track for $1 Trillion in 2026

key_facts.fact: Global semiconductor sales reached $88.8 billion in February 2026, up 7.6% from January's $82.5 billion and 61.8% higher than February 2025's $54.9 billion.
Regional year-over-year sales: Asia Pacific +93.5%, Americas +59.2%, China +57.4%, Europe +42.3%, Japan -0.3%.
SIA President John Neuffer said strong global demand is expected to persist, with annual sales projected to reach roughly $1 trillion globally in 2026.
The semiconductor industry on track to hit $1 trillion in sales in 2026, following a $791.7 billion haul in 2025.

stories.headline: Chinese Chipmakers Report Record 2025 Revenues as Domestic AI Chip Share Hits 41% of Market

key_facts.fact: China's largest chipmaker SMIC reported 2025 revenue rose 16% YoY to a record $9.3 billion; analysts expect it could top $11 billion in 2026.
Domestic vendors shipped 1.65 million AI accelerator cards in 2025, capturing 41% of the Chinese market and closing in on Nvidia's 55% share, according to IDC data.
Huawei shipped 812,000 AI chips in 2025, emerging as the leading Chinese AI chip supplier amid US export controls.
CXMT's revenue jumped about 130% to ¥55 billion; Moore Threads guided 2025 revenue of ¥1.45-1.52 billion, a 231-247% YoY increase.
Record revenues were driven by AI demand, memory shortages, and US export restrictions that pushed Beijing to favor domestic suppliers.

stories.headline: ULA Launches 29 Amazon Leo Satellites on Heaviest Atlas V Payload Ever From Cape Canaveral

key_facts.fact: The LA-05 mission launched at 1:46 a.m. ET on April 4, 2026 from Space Launch Complex-41 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station aboard a ULA Atlas V 551 rocket.
The mission deployed 29 Amazon Leo internet satellites, making it the heaviest payload ever launched by an Atlas V rocket.
Joint engineering between Amazon and ULA enabled a new four-tier dispenser configuration and Centaur upper stage updates to increase from previous payloads to 29 satellites.
Amazon Leo (formerly Project Kuiper) is building a constellation of 3,236 satellites to provide broadband internet access, with a mid-year FCC deadline to grow to ~1,600 satellites.

stories.headline: US-Israeli Strikes Destroy Tehran's Century-Old Pasteur Institute on Day 35 of Iran War

key_facts.fact: US and Israeli forces struck Iran's Pasteur Institute, a century-old medical research center founded in 1920, rendering it unable to continue delivering health services according to the WHO.

WHO Director General Tedros said the Pasteur Institute played 'an important role in protecting and promoting population health, including in emergencies,' with two departments serving as WHO collaborating centres.
WHO has verified at least 20 attacks on Iran's healthcare system since March 1, causing nine deaths including frontline health and Red Crescent workers.
At least 2,076 people have been killed and 26,500 wounded in Iran since the war began on February 28, with over 600 schools and education centers damaged.
A drone strike also hit a Red Crescent aid warehouse in Bushehr province on the same day.

US officials stated a bridge struck near Tehran was 'used to transport material for Iranian military drones,' though Iran contested this, claiming it was civilian infrastructure protected under international law.

stories.headline: Iran Strikes Kuwait's Al-Ahmadi Refinery and UAE's Habshan Gas Plant in Escalating Gulf Campaign

key_facts.fact: Iranian drones struck Kuwait's Mina Al-Ahmadi refinery on April 3, igniting fires in multiple operational units, marking the third time the facility has been targeted since the war began.
A separate strike hit a Kuwaiti power and desalination plant before midday Friday, threatening water supply in a nation highly dependent on desalinated water.
Iran also struck the UAE's Habshan gas facility, the country's largest gas complex, which was shut down for the second time in 15 days.
The UAE intercepted 19 ballistic missiles and 26 drones on the prior day, with 12 people injured from falling debris (7 Nepali, 5 Indian nationals).
The IRGC denied responsibility for the Kuwait desalination plant strike, instead blaming Israel for 'unconditional and illegitimate attack on Kuwait's water desalination centres.'

stories.headline: UK-Led 40-Nation Meeting Calls for Immediate Strait of Hormuz Reopening but Reaches No Agreement

key_facts.fact: Over 40 countries and international organizations including the IMO and EU attended a UK-hosted virtual meeting on April 3 to discuss reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper convened the meeting, which called for 'the immediate and unconditional reopening of the Strait.'

Participants discussed increasing diplomatic pressure and sanctions on Iran, releasing trapped ships and sailors, and rejecting Iran's attempts to impose tolls on vessels, but reached no concrete agreement.
France pushed back on calls to force open the Strait, with Macron trading barbs with Trump over the approach to the crisis.

stories.headline: Russia, China, and France Triple Veto Blocks UN Resolution to Authorize Force to Reopen Strait of Hormuz

key_facts.fact: Russia, China, and France vetoed a UN Security Council resolution proposed by Bahrain and backed by Gulf states and Jordan that would have authorized 'defensive measures' to secure transit through the Strait of Hormuz.
The three vetoing nations cited 'principled opposition to any language authorising force' as their reason for blocking the initiative.
The veto effectively permits Iran to continue restricting oil and goods flow through the strategic waterway without international military intervention.
The US and Israel continue military operations against Iran while rejecting ceasefire proposals, creating a contrast with the Security Council's inability to authorize collective action on shipping.

stories.headline: Oil Crisis Morphs Into 'Everything Crisis' as Petrochemical Shortages Hit Medical Supplies and Food

key_facts.fact: The Strait of Hormuz closure has reduced global crude oil supply by approximately one-fifth, squeezing not just fuel but petrochemicals needed for everyday items.
Plastic resin prices in Asia have risen up to 59% since late February, polyester chip prices jumped roughly 50%, and plastic bottle cap costs have quadrupled.
The Middle East produces 17% of world naphtha, 30% of plastic resin, 45% of sulfur, 33% of helium, and 22% of urea/ammonia — all now in short supply.
Japan faces fears that patients with chronic kidney failure won't get treatment due to shortages of plastic hemodialysis tubes; Malaysian glove manufacturers report latex shortages.
J.P. Morgan analysts warned that supply constraints will intensify in April, saying 'the primary challenge has shifted from price to physical scarcity.'

stories.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth Fires Army Chief of Staff Gen. Randy George and Two Generals During Iran War

key_facts.fact: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth forced out Army Chief of Staff General Randy A. George, the 41st person to hold the post, along with Gen. David Hodne (head of Army Transformation and Training Command) and Maj. Gen. William Green Jr. (Army Chief of Chaplains).

The New York Times reported the removal stemmed from clashes over Hegseth's decision to block promotions for four Army officers — two Black, two women — on a list of 29 personnel. George requested a meeting to discuss potential bias two weeks earlier, but Hegseth refused.
Christopher LaNeve, a former Hegseth military aide, is expected to serve as acting chief of staff.
Democratic Senator Chris Murphy said 'experienced generals are telling Hegseth his Iran war plans are unworkable, disastrous, and deadly.'

stories.headline: Artemis II Crew Passes Halfway Point to Moon, Prepares for First Lunar Flyby Since 1972

key_facts.fact: The Artemis II crew — Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialists Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen (CSA) — passed the halfway point to the Moon on Flight Day 3.
This is the first time humans have departed Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972; the crew completed the translunar injection burn on Flight Day 2 to break free of Earth's orbit.
Astronaut Christina Koch reported: 'We can see the Moon out of the docking hatch right now. It's a beautiful sight.'
The crew is preparing the Orion spacecraft cabin for a lunar flyby planned for Monday, April 6, when they will photograph areas of the far side of the Moon never seen directly by humans.
The first outbound trajectory correction burn was cancelled, indicating the spacecraft is on an accurate course toward the Moon.
